item: Victorian brown transfer-printed ironstone dinner service in the 'Sydney' pattern (urn with flowers and a ewer in the centre, Greek-key/shell-and-anthemion border). Backstamp reads SYDNEY in an octagonal cartouche with a pattern letter. Per a Casey & Lowe ceramic report, 'Sydney' is one of four transfer patterns (Chantilly, Corsina, Sydenham, Sydney) attributed to John Thomson (& Sons), Glasgow Scotland, so likely Scottish export ware of c.1860s-80s that sold into Australia. Owner's handwritten note: Brown Transfer Dinner Set, 6 dinner plates, 9 B/B (bread and butter) plates, 7 soup plates, 1 medium serving platter, 1 small platter (23 pieces).
note: Antique pair, Georgian/19thC brown transferware mourning plates (older, different pattern); excludes postage

item: Set of 10 Murano (Venetian) vaseline/uranium glass stemware, c.1920s-50s: 3 coupes (champagne/cocktail) with spiral-ribbed pale yellow-green uranium bowl and foot and a pink/rose aventurine (gold-fleck) dolphin stem with black-dot eyes on a uranium knop; and 7 tall conical goblets/vases in pale green uranium glass with a gold-foil (aventurine) ribbed knop and plain foot. Coupe glows bright green under UV in photo 2; goblet glows in photo 3. This dolphin-stem coupe form is the classic Salviati/Venice & Murano Glass Co type and was made by several Murano firms (Salviati, Cenedese, Toso). Unmarked, which is normal for Salviati table glass (paper labels only). So: Salviati-TYPE Murano, not provable as Salviati.
note: 8 Salviati pale green ribbed-bowl martini/champagne glasses with gold-fleck dolphin stems c.1960. Closest match to our 3 coupes (ours are vaseline/uranium yellow-green with pink-gold dolphins). About US$75 a glass. Over 3 years old.

item: Four miniature vaseline (uranium, yellow) pressed glass animal-on-nest covered salt dishes, about 6-8 cm long: a cat on nest, a hen on nest, a turkey on nest and a dog (Scottie/terrier type) on nest, each with a scalloped basketweave base. These are the 'hen on nest' style novelty salts made in the 1970s-2000s by US makers such as Boyd, Degenhart, Mosser, Summit and Westmoreland, not Victorian. Plus two vaseline glass eye baths (eye wash cups): one clear vaseline with banded rim on a short pedestal, and one taller vaseline with a white opalescent rim on a stem foot. Catalogue says one tureen chipped. 'EYE GLASSES' in the catalogue means eye baths. Update after Lens: the cat on nest is the same mould as a Mosser Glass (Cambridge, Ohio) miniature cat on nest sold on eBay; the lacy scalloped bases on all four look like one maker's series, most likely Mosser miniatures (Boyd makes similar mini turkey and Scottie salts). Made from the 1970s onward, not antique.
note: Vintage Mosser miniature cat on nest, vaseline glass. Same mould as our cat (lacy base). Accepted price confirmed on the item page.

item: Original watercolour (possibly with gutta or masking resist giving the white outlines; she also paints on silk) of five whimsical stylised cats with flowers and a small bird on a purple-blue wash ground, signed 'Evelyn Antonysen' in white lower right. Image about 18 x 24 cm, gold slip, green mount, gilt rope-moulded frame with green marble-effect inner band, under glass. Evelyn Antonysen is a living North-West Tasmanian artist and art teacher (Forth, later Ulverstone; galleries in Penguin; Deloraine Craft Fair since 1996; Australian Society for Miniature Art committee). Her known work is mainly Tasmanian coastal landscapes; whimsical cats are not her usual line. She also sells reproductions and cards, so it may be a print. Current bid A$50, estimate 30-40.

item: Haig's Dimple 'Superior de luxe Scotch Whisky' ceramic souvenir decanter for the 1987 America's Cup defence, 'Fremantle Western Australia 1987', white glazed porcelain with gilt laurel, two crossed sails and the flags of seven challenger/defender nations (Australia, Italy, UK, USA, Canada, New Zealand, France); Dimple arms on the reverse. item: Oil on board or canvas, portrait format, framed in a modern gilt moulding with grey linen slip. Evening/dusk bush river scene: tall dead eucalypts with hanging bark at left, dense bush, yellow sunset band, still water with reflections in the foreground. Catalogue: ERNEST CHRISTMAS ATTRIBUTED OIL EVENING ON THE YARRA RIVER H-35 W-25 CM. Style (dark tonal bush river at dusk, gold sky band) is consistent with the late Victorian Australian bush-river genre that Ernest William Christmas (1863-1918, born Adelaide, worked Victoria/NSW, then NZ and Hawaii) painted, but it is a common genre. Ernest Christmas was not a Tasmanian painter, the lot note has that wrong.
note: Last Glow Over the River 1890, oil on board, initialled and dated E W C / 90, 34 x 50 cm. Dusk river subject very like lot 793, est A$400-600, sold under estimate. Price read on Gibson's own lot page.

item: Three handmade soft red clay bricks (not 'items' of metal: the catalogue lot is '3 BROAD ARROW STAMPED CONVICT BRICKS - EX-ALANVALE NEWNHAM', i.e. bricks recovered from Alanvale, Newnham, Launceston). Each has marks hand-incised into the wet clay before firing (drawn with a finger or stick, not a stamped frog): brick 1 (larger, paler, mortar on one edge) reads roughly 'L ^ D' with a broad arrow between letters; brick 2 has a single vertical stroke beside a large broad arrow; brick 3 reads roughly 'W ^ W' (or W ^ M) with a broad arrow in the middle. Bricks 2 and 3 also show deep finger/thumb impressions at the corners, the classic sign of hand moulding seen on Tasmanian convict-made bricks. These are consistent with genuine colonial (convict-era, c.1820s-1850s) Van Diemen's Land government bricks: broad arrow plus moulder's/gang initials scratched by hand is the typical Tasmanian convict pattern; later government issue used stamped marks in a frog, not hand scratching. Provenance (Alanvale) cannot be verified from photos. Bulky-ish and heavy (3 bricks, perhaps 9-10 kg).
note: Tasmanian convict brick incised 'E D' and broad arrow, with fingerprint, 1840s, 225 mm, chips and splits. Est A$50-75. Same type as these (initials plus broad arrow plus finger marks). Over 3 years old.

item: Cast iron wall-mounted yoke bell (farm / dinner / school style), approx 30 cm mouth diameter, 50 cm overall height. Wall plate with 4 bolt holes, U-shaped hanging bracket, pivoting yoke with acorn finial, swinging pull arm for a rope, iron clapper tied with twine. Black painted finish, light rust at pivots. Pattern matches the common US farm-bell format (C.S. Bell / Hillsboro style) and the many later reproductions. Catalogue: estimate A$150-250; current bid A$220 at 10 Nov. Google Lens on photo 1: closest matches are modern 'antique style' cast iron school/dinner bells, eg The Renmy Store 'Large Cast Iron School Dinner Bell' 51 cm H x 38 cm W, 8.7 kg, A$239.95 new (same wall plate, U bracket, yoke, acorn finial and rope arm, though the lot's plate has 4 holes and a chamfered top). The clean casting, absence of any foundry name or 'No.' size mark and the twine-tied clapper point to a 20th/21st century reproduction rather than a 19th century C.S. Bell, Crystal Metal or similar US foundry bell (those carry cast names, size numbers and 1886 patent dates on the yoke). Estimated weight 8-12 kg.
note: Used 1990s cast iron 12.5in farmhouse dinner bell with bracket; 7 sold at this price

item: Victorian manuscript household and commonplace book in a full calf binding (blind and gilt ruled boards with fleuron corner tools, raised bands and fleurons on the spine), with an alphabetical cut thumb index down the fore-edge. Neat ink entries seen: 'Gooseberry Fool' recipe; a long 'Games' section of parlour games (Twenty Questions, Geography, Birds Beasts and Fishes, and others); a 'Galls ...' remedy; and a dated 'Gun Powder' entry (August 188?, reads as 1884) recording a trial of Curtis & Harvey's Diamond Grain black powder against White Schultze smokeless powder in a gun, with penetration figures. Loose items tucked in: a handwritten letter on blue-lined paper, a pencil landscape sketch of figures in a rural scene, a printed blue certificate or notice ('We hereby ...', signed), an envelope with a red stamp and postmarks, and other loose blue sheets. English household, about 1870-1890 judging by the hand, Curtis & Harvey and Schultze references. No owner name or place legible in the photos. Cloud scan is broadly right.
note: 1842 Victorian leather commonplace book album, Barbara Poore manuscript. Sold at list (or Best Offer listing).

item: American 'acorn' shelf clock, J.C. Brown / Forestville Manufacturing Co, Bristol (Forestville) Connecticut, c.1847-50. Laminated (bent-ply) rosewood/mahogany-look acorn-form case with laminated side arms and turned acorn finials on a stepped base, 65 cm high. Pointed upper door glass over a painted zinc dial (Roman numerals, pink-rose and gilt-leaf spandrels, no maker name visible on the dial in the photo), lower door with frosted/etched glass tablet in a feather-and-cross pattern with small coloured roundels. Inside: brass bell, brass-covered pendulum bob, and a torn printed paper label 'CLOCK MANUFACTORY / J. C. BROWN' with a woodcut vignette and text columns, the backboard paper mostly torn away. A brass fitting at the base, which could be the top of the detached fusees or a winding key. Looks period, not a modern copy, but this can't be confirmed from three 450x600 photos.
note: 'Antique c.1845 J.C. Brown 24" 8-Day Acorn Shelf Clock w/Terry & Andrews Mvt' (movement probably not the original Forestville one), fixed price, postage A$83. Terapeak row with link; listing page returned eBay error, not opened.

item: Tray of mixed small items: (1) gilt star-shaped 'REWARD OF MERIT' prize medal with blue enamel band and plain centre, on a ring (likely gilt base metal, possibly gold; unproven); (2) round open crescent-and-flower brooch, rose-coloured metal set with seed pearls and a small green stone (Edwardian style, likely 9ct but unmarked in photo); (3) yellow gold ribbon-twist bar brooch with an oval blue/green opal (solid or doublet); (4) repousse double-flower bar brooch with two red stones (Victorian style, probably pinchbeck/rolled gold); (5) small rose-gold ring with a turquoise and white-stone cluster in a Taylors Jewellers (3 Centenary Arcade, Launceston) bag, with a handwritten note that appears to say the jeweller could not repair it; (6) worn white-metal medal/coin pendant with loop (figure design, illegible); (7) white-metal 'Exhibition Building' medalet dated 1880 (Melbourne International Exhibition type) and two smaller white-metal arms medalets; (8) enamel badges: heart-shaped 'SEMPER PARATUS' Registered General Nurse of Tasmania badge (orange Maltese cross), round 'MISERIS SUCCURRERE DISCO' nurse badge with red centre lettered L?H (probably LGH, Launceston General Hospital), IOOF 'FLT' Odd Fellows badge, and a round enamel 'FLT' badge with eye/triangle; (9) hat pin with pine-cone/thistle style head stuck in a cork.
note: Antique 9ct floral spray brooch with 9 seed pearls and one stone, auction. Guide for the crescent/flower seed pearl brooch if 9ct.

item: John Campbell Pottery, Launceston. Shield-shaped wall pocket, catalogue height 18 cm (other examples measured 18 to 18.5 x 14.5 x 5.5 cm). Front: mottled emerald to aqua green glaze; relief koala in treacle brown clinging to a gum branch, two brown gumnuts above, leaves picked out in ochre yellow. Back: flat, olive yellow-green glaze with darker green runs at the edges, three stilt marks. No shape number, no date. The koala, nuts, branch and leaves are identical on the ten other examples I compared (Leski 2024 and 2026, Mossgreen 2009 x2 and 2016, Shapiro 2007 and 2015, Gowans 2011, eBay 2025 and 2026, Albion 2026), so the decoration is moulded, not hand-modelled; only the glaze colours change. Made after John Campbell's death in 1929, when his son Colin ran the pottery: about 1930s to 1950s. No dated example found. Condition from photos: pale angular marks on the front near the top rim, left of the gumnuts (possible glaze flake or chip, could be reflections); a dark brown spot on the side edge (right side from the front, left from the back): chip, kiln mark or glaze burn. No crack visible. Current bid $200 on 28 Nov 2026.
note: Green with brown koala, 18 cm, same colourway as lot 657. Hammer; premium 21.45% on top. Provenance The Gary & Genevieve Morgan Collection. One week old.

item: Donald Friend (1915-1989), '3 Nudes', Bali period (he lived in Bali from 1968 to 1980), undated. Three standing nude male youths, adolescent in appearance: two at left facing each other in profile, one at right facing front with a hand raised to the shoulder. Pen and black ink with dense hatching, ochre and orange watercolour wash, opaque white gouache highlights, pale blue-grey gouache ground and a pinkish-buff floor band, on paper. Catalogue size 73 x 48 cm. The photo geometry fits that being the sight size, with the frame about 96 x 71 cm, but it is not confirmed. Gold reeded frame, double mat (beige outer, grey inner), glazed. Condition from photos: a few grey-brown spots lower centre and fine specks lower right (possible foxing or mould); no tears or creases visible; fading cannot be judged. No bid yet on 28 Nov 2026 (opens at $1,000).
note: 'Nude Studies': three nude youths, pen and brown ink and gouache, 75 x 49 cm, signed lower left Donald Friend / Bali, inscribed 'For Attilio, Dec. '74'. Hammer; premium 25% plus tax on top.
